reading.title: 奶奶的元宵
reading.zh: 每年正月十五元宵节，是我们家最热闹的日子。这一天，在外地工作的叔叔、姑姑都会赶回老家，围坐在奶奶身边，吃她亲手包的元宵。奶奶今年八十多岁了，脸上总是带着慈祥的笑容。她操劳了一辈子，年轻时既要下地干活，又要照顾一大家子人，对每个孩子都关心得无微不至。小时候，我最巴不得过年，因为奶奶会做一桌家常佳肴，还会偷偷塞给我零花钱。我嘴馋，常常还没开饭就溜进厨房偷吃，奶奶看见了也不生气，只是笑着叮嘱我：“慢点儿吃，别烫着。”奶奶没上过几年学，认识的字不多，却特别重视孩子们的品行。她常说：“做人要能吃苦，要诚实，别人帮过你，你要记一辈子。”在她的熏陶下，我们这一代人虽然各自在不同的城市生活，却都保持着勤俭、厚道的家风。前年冬天，奶奶摔了一跤，从此只能拄着拐杖走路。不料第二年元宵节前，她又执意要自己包元宵。妈妈屡次劝她休息，她却说：“手艺这东西，不用就生疏了。”那天她站在厨房里，手冻得直哆嗦，断断续续包了一下午。吃饭时，她挎着一个小篮子，把元宵一个个分到我们碗里。那一刹那，我忽然恍然大悟：奶奶包的哪里只是元宵，分明是她对这个家全部的爱。我低下头，不禁热泪盈眶。如今我也成了家。每当工作遇到困难，我就会想起奶奶的话。归根到底，一个家庭最宝贵的财富，不是钱，而是代代相传的温暖与品格。有了它，我们走到哪里都没有后顾之忧。
reading.en: Every year on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month, the Lantern Festival, is the liveliest day in our family. On that day my uncles and aunts who work in other cities hurry back to our hometown and sit around Grandma to eat the sweet dumplings she makes by hand. Grandma is over eighty now, and her face always wears a kind smile. She worked hard all her life: when she was young she had to work in the fields and look after a big family, and she cared for every child in every possible way. As a child, I couldn't wait for New Year, because Grandma would cook a table full of homestyle dishes and secretly slip me pocket money. I was greedy and often sneaked into the kitchen to snack before dinner was served; when Grandma saw me she never got angry, but just smiled and reminded me: "Eat slowly, don't burn yourself." Grandma only went to school for a few years and knows few characters, but she has always placed great importance on the children's character. She often says: "To be a good person you must be able to bear hardship and be honest; if someone has helped you, remember it all your life." Under her influence, though we of my generation live in different cities, we have all kept the family tradition of being hardworking, thrifty and kind-hearted. The winter before last, Grandma had a fall, and since then she can only walk with a cane. Unexpectedly, before the next Lantern Festival, she insisted on making the dumplings herself. Mom repeatedly urged her to rest, but she said: "A skill like this gets rusty if you don't use it." That day she stood in the kitchen, her hands trembling with cold, making dumplings on and off all afternoon. At dinner, with a small basket on her arm, she put the dumplings into our bowls one by one. In that instant it suddenly dawned on me: what Grandma was wrapping was not just dumplings, but clearly all her love for this family. I lowered my head, and my eyes filled with tears. Now I have a family of my own. Whenever I run into difficulties at work, I remember Grandma's words. In the end, a family's most precious wealth is not money but the warmth and character passed down from generation to generation. With that, wherever we go, we have nothing to worry about.

grammar.title: Idioms as adverbials: 成语 + 地 + 动词
grammar.pattern: 主语 + 兴致勃勃 / 聚精会神 / 争先恐后 + 地 + 动词
grammar.explain: Many four-character idioms describe a manner and can go before a verb with 地, like ordinary adverbials. This makes writing vivid. Common examples are 兴致勃勃 'in high spirits', 聚精会神 'with full attention' and 争先恐后 'vying to be first'.

grammar.title: Idioms for evaluation: 一举两得 / 得不偿失
grammar.pattern: 这样做 + 是 / 可谓 + 一举两得 / 得不偿失
grammar.explain: Idioms often sum up a judgment at the end of a sentence. 一举两得 'kill two birds with one stone' praises a choice with two benefits; 得不偿失 'the loss outweighs the gain' criticizes one. 可谓 'can be called' is a formal way to introduce them.

grammar.title: Describing rapid change: 与日俱增 / 日新月异

grammar.explain: Both idioms describe fast change. 与日俱增 'grow day by day' is used with feelings, numbers or pressure. 日新月异 'change with each passing day' describes the rapid development of cities, technology and society.

reading.title: 欢迎来到我的家乡
reading.zh: 我的家乡位于中国南方，是一个山清水秀的省份。全省地势西高东低：西部是连绵的山区，山峰陡峭，森林茂盛；中部以丘陵为主；东部则是一片平原，土地肥沃，盛产稻谷和茶叶。一条大河自西向东流过全省，沿途汇集了几十条支流，被当地人亲切地称为“母亲河”。过去，这条河时常泛滥，给两岸的百姓带来了不少灾难。几十年来，当地政府组织群众修建了坚固的堤坝和大量水利设施，彻底改变了“十年九涝”的局面。如今，这里连年丰收，人们安居乐业。西部山区还利用草场资源发展畜牧业，牛羊成群，一派欣欣向荣的景象。省会城市更是日新月异。高楼拔地而起，地铁四通八达，古老的街巷和现代化的商业区和谐并存。每到周末，人们兴致勃勃地去逛夜市，那里的小吃物美价廉，一条街走下来就能品尝几十种地方风味。家乡人热情好客。如果你到农村做客，主人一定会盛情款待，拿出最好的酒菜招待你。春节期间，大家走亲访友、互相拜年，孩子们则争先恐后地给长辈磕头，领取压岁钱。近年来，不少村子把传统节日和乡村旅游结合起来，既保留了民俗，又增加了收入，可谓一举两得。欢迎你来我的家乡看看，我相信，这里的山水和人情一定会让你流连忘返。
reading.en: My hometown is in southern China, in a province of green hills and clear waters. The terrain is high in the west and low in the east: the west is a stretch of mountains with steep peaks and lush forests; the center is mostly hilly; and the east is a plain with fertile soil that produces abundant rice and tea. A great river flows across the province from west to east, gathering dozens of tributaries along the way, and the locals affectionately call it the "Mother River". In the past, this river often flooded, bringing many disasters to the people on its banks. Over the decades, the local government organized people to build sturdy dikes and many water conservancy works, completely ending the situation of "floods in nine years out of ten". Today there are good harvests year after year, and people live in peace and work happily. The western mountains also use their grasslands to develop animal husbandry; with herds of cattle and sheep everywhere, the whole area is thriving. The provincial capital changes with each passing day. Tall buildings rise from the ground, the subway reaches every corner, and old streets and alleys coexist harmoniously with modern commercial districts. Every weekend, people go to the night markets in high spirits; the snacks there are good and cheap, and in a single street you can sample dozens of local specialties. The people of my hometown are warm and hospitable. If you visit a village home, your hosts will treat you with great kindness and bring out their best food and drink. During the Spring Festival, people visit relatives and friends and exchange New Year greetings, while children vie with each other to kowtow to their elders and receive lucky money. In recent years, many villages have combined traditional festivals with rural tourism, preserving folk customs while increasing income — two birds with one stone. You are welcome to come and see my hometown. I'm sure its landscapes and its people will make you want to stay.

grammar.title: Modest replies to praise: 过奖 / 不敢当
grammar.pattern: 别人称赞你 → 过奖 了 / 不敢当 / 哪里 哪里
grammar.explain: When praised, Chinese etiquette expects a modest reply rather than simply "thank you". 过奖了 'you flatter me' and 不敢当 'I don't deserve it' are polite and slightly formal; 哪里哪里 is more casual. 不敢当 is also used when someone shows you great respect.

examples.zh: 您 过奖 了 ， 我 做 得 还 很 不够 。
examples.en: You flatter me — I still have a long way to go.

examples.zh: “ 您 是 这 方面 的 泰斗 。 ” “ 不敢当 ， 不敢当 。 ”
examples.en: "You're the leading authority in this field." "Oh, I don't deserve that."

grammar.title: Idioms from fables: 画蛇添足 / 拔苗助长
grammar.pattern: （这样做）+ 就是 / 无异于 + 成语
grammar.explain: Many chengyu come from ancient fables and are used to criticize a way of acting. 画蛇添足 'draw legs on a snake' means spoiling something by overdoing it; 拔苗助长 'pull up seedlings to help them grow' means doing harm through impatience. They usually act as the predicate after 是 or 无异于 'is no different from'.

examples.zh: 文章 已经 很 好 了 ， 再 加 这 段 就是 画蛇添足 。
examples.en: The essay is already good; adding this paragraph would be overdoing it.

examples.zh: 逼 孩子 每 天 学习 十几 个 小时 ， 无异于 拔苗助长 。
examples.en: Forcing children to study a dozen hours a day is like pulling up seedlings to make them grow.

grammar.title: Literary 'would rather' and 'if': 宁肯 / 假使
grammar.pattern: 宁肯 + A ， 也 不 + B ； 假使 + 条件 ， …
grammar.explain: 宁肯 is a literary synonym of 宁愿 and 宁可 'would rather'. 假使 is a literary 'if', like 倘若 and 假如. Both are typical of written Chinese and formal speech.

examples.zh: 我 宁肯 自己 吃亏 ， 也 不 愿意 欺骗 别人 。
examples.en: I'd rather lose out myself than deceive others.

examples.zh: 假使 没有 大家 的 帮助 ， 我 不 可能 成功 。
examples.en: Without everyone's help, I could never have succeeded.

reading.title: 我的中国见闻
reading.zh: 来中国留学三年，我把自己的见闻写成了一本小书。在序言里，我想先说一说这几年最深的感受：中国文化真是博大精深。刚来的时候，我对这里的风土人情一无所知，闹了不少笑话。第一次去中国朋友家做客，主人夸我汉语说得好，我高兴地回答“谢谢”，后来才知道，更地道的说法是“过奖了”或者“不敢当”。还有一次，朋友请我吃饭，我抢着付钱，朋友坚持说：“你是客人，今天我做东！”我这才明白，在中国，抢着请客是热情的表现。学汉字也让我吃了不少苦头。我先学的是繁体字，后来发现大陆普遍使用简体字，只好从头再来。刚开始，我急于求成，每天抄写几百个字，结果越学越乱。我的老师勉励我说：“学语言就像种庄稼，拔苗助长是不行的，要锲而不舍，一步一步来。”最让我着迷的是中国的传统节日。春节贴对联、吃饺子，端午节赛龙舟、包粽子，重阳节登高、看望老人……每个节日都按农历来过，背后都有一个动人的故事。去年春节，我在一位老师家里过年，看着祖孙三代围坐在一起，津津有味地吃着年夜饭，我第一次体会到什么叫“天伦之乐”。三年来，我去过很多举世闻名的地方，也逛过街头卖糖葫芦的小摊儿。我发现，越是了解中国，越觉得自己需要学习的东西很多，真是任重道远。这本小书谈不上精益求精，但字字都是真心话。谨以此书，感谢所有帮助过我的中国朋友，感谢这份深情厚谊。
reading.en: After three years of studying in China, I have turned what I saw and heard into a little book. In this preface, I would like first to share my strongest impression of these years: Chinese culture is truly broad and profound. When I first arrived, I knew nothing about local customs and made plenty of blunders. The first time I visited a Chinese friend's home, my host praised my Chinese, and I happily replied "thank you"; only later did I learn that the more natural reply would be "you flatter me" or "I don't deserve it". Another time, when a friend invited me to dinner, I rushed to pay, but my friend insisted: "You're the guest — today it's my treat!" Only then did I understand that in China, competing to pay is a sign of warmth. Learning Chinese characters also gave me a hard time. I learned traditional characters first, then found that simplified characters are used throughout the mainland, so I had to start again from scratch. At first I wanted quick results and copied out hundreds of characters a day, but the more I learned, the more confused I became. My teacher encouraged me: "Learning a language is like growing crops. Pulling up the seedlings to help them grow won't work — you have to persevere, one step at a time." What fascinates me most are China's traditional festivals: pasting up couplets and eating dumplings at Spring Festival, dragon-boat races and zongzi at the Dragon Boat Festival, climbing hills and visiting the elderly at the Double Ninth Festival... Every festival follows the lunar calendar and has a moving story behind it. Last Spring Festival, I celebrated at a teacher's home, and watching three generations sitting together, relishing their New Year's Eve dinner, I understood for the first time what "the joy of family life" means. In these three years I have visited many world-famous places and also wandered past street stalls selling candied haws. I've found that the more I learn about China, the more I feel there is to learn — the road ahead is long indeed. This little book is far from polished, but every word comes from the heart. I dedicate it to all the Chinese friends who have helped me, in gratitude for their deep friendship.

questions.q: 作者第一次被夸汉语好时，为什么后来觉得自己的回答不够地道？
questions.qEn: Why did the author later feel his reply to praise of his Chinese was not quite natural?
options: 中国人习惯用“过奖了”“不敢当”等谦虚的说法

questions.q: 老师用“拔苗助长”想提醒作者什么？
questions.qEn: What was the teacher warning the author against with "拔苗助长"?
options: 学语言不能急于求成，要坚持一步步来

questions.q: 作者在老师家过春节时体会到了什么？
questions.qEn: What did the author experience at his teacher's home during Spring Festival?
options: 一家人团聚的天伦之乐
